chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: The reciters are three. One who recites the Quran to gain favor with the kings and to become haughty with the people; he is from the people of Hell. And one who recites the Quran, memorizes its letters but neglects its limits; he is from the people of Hell. And one who recites the Quran and conceals himself beneath his cloak; he acts according to its clear verses, believes in its similar ones, establishes its obligations, makes halal what it has made halal, and makes haram what it has made haram. This is one of those whom God saved from the misguiding trials, and he is from the people of Paradise, and he intercedes for whom he wishes.

key_terms.لِيَسْتَدِرَّ بِهِ الْمُلُوكَ: to gain favor with the kings
key_terms.وَيَسْطِيلَ بِهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ: and to become haughty with the people

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Quran reciters and their ultimate fate according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes Quran reciters into three distinct groups based on their spiritual and practical engagement with the text. The first two are condemned: one who uses the Quran for political dominance and arrogance, and another who memorizes the letters but neglects the legal and ethical boundaries (hudud). The third group, who internalize the text by acting upon the clear verses (muhkamat) and believing in the complex ones (mutashabihat), are saved from trials and granted intercession.
